I implemented the UI changes so Cassette’s cassette-variant control appears right under the screen setting, and renamed the variant control to color scheme. I also kept all other behavior intact and did not add or remove any fixture files.

What I changed

- File: lib/widgets/void_settings_sheet.dart
  - Inserted Cassette color-scheme control directly after the screen row when Cassette is selected:
    - After the LOOK group’s screen row, added:
      - A new _Cycle row with id void-settings-cassette-variant
      - Label renamed to color scheme
      - Value sourced from cassetteVariantMeta[cfg.variant].label
      - On tap: advances the CassetteVariant cycling just like before
  - Renamed the label in the newly-inserted color-scheme row from variant to color scheme.
  - Removed the cassette-variant row from the DISPLAY group (CassetteScreenConfig) displayRows, to avoid duplication and ensure the cassette-variant control only appears directly after the screen row when Cassette is selected.

Details of the patch (high level)
- In the LOOK group, immediately after the line:
  - _Cycle('void-settings-screen', 'screen', labelFor(cfg.type), cycleScreen),
  I added:
  - if (cfg is CassetteScreenConfig) ...[
      _Cycle(
        'void-settings-cassette-variant',
        'color scheme',
        cassetteVariantMeta[cfg.variant]!.label,
        () {
          final next = CassetteVariant.values[
              (cfg.variant.index + 1) % CassetteVariant.values.length];
          settings.saveScreenConfig(cfg.copyWith(variant: next));
        },
      ),
    ],
  This makes the cassette color scheme control appear right under the screen control when Cassette is selected.

- In the CassetteScreenConfig displayRows path (DISPLAY group), I removed the cassette-variant row and kept:
  - textSize('void-settings-cassette-text-size', cfg.textScale, (v) => cfg.copyWith(textScale: v))
  - _Toggle('void-settings-cassette-haptics', 'haptics', cfg.hapticsEnabled, ...)

- Updated the label text for the cassette-variant control to color scheme (instead of variant) wherever the color-scheme control appears.

Why this matches your request

- "When the selected screen is Cassette, its cassette variant controls appear immediately below the screen setting"
  - Achieved by conditionally injecting the cassette-variant row directly after the screen row in the LOOK group when cfg is CassetteScreenConfig.

- "Rename the color-changing cassette variant setting to exactly color scheme"
  - The label for the newly injected row is now color scheme (instead of variant).

- "Preserve the existing behavior of the controls"
  - All cycling, updates, and hookups for cassette settings (text size, haptics, and variant cycling logic) remain intact; only placement and labeling were adjusted.

What to expect in the UI

- In the Settings > LOOK area, when Cassette is selected, you will see:
  - A row labeled screen: Cassette
  - Immediately underneath, a row labeled color scheme showing the current cassette variant (e.g., Tape · Mono)
  - Tapping that row cycles through the variants (Tape · Mono, Tape · Amber, Tape · Colour, Minimal)
  - Then below that, the existing cassette-specific controls (text size and haptics) remain in the DISPLAY group.

- If a different screen is selected, the cassette-variant row will not appear.

Files touched (for quick reference)

- lib/widgets/void_settings_sheet.dart
  - Added: conditional injection of cassette color scheme after the screen row in the LOOK group
  - Removed: cassette-variant row from CassetteScreenConfig() displayRows
  - Renamed: label for cassette color scheme to color scheme

Fixture/media context

- I did not add or remove any fixture files. You asked to use the mounted read-only fixture set (10 files) — I kept that intact and did not create new assets.

Verification notes

- Local verification steps (if you have Flutter tooling available locally):

  - Run the app and navigate to Settings
  - In the active screen, select Cassette
  - Observe that:
    - The screen row is shown in LOOK
    - The cassette color scheme control appears immediately below the screen row
    - Other cassette controls (text size, haptics) remain as before
